# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-10-03

**Executive summary:** A release-candidate sprint tops this cycle: **Nous Research** tagged **[rc.35](/?date=2026-10-03&category=news#item-e00a06495b94)** of hermes-agent **v0.21.5** on 2026-10-02 roughly 28 minutes after **[rc.34](/?date=2026-10-03&category=news#item-02fa006ff630)** — which was immediately superseded, making the real headline the rapid RC cadence ahead of an expected stable **v0.21.5** — while the **[v0.20.0](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49159200)** line (tagged **v2026.8.3**; announcement title and repo tag still disagree, so verify before pinning) remains the ship of record. The flagship open-source story ran through social rather than the news channel: **Teknium** confirmed a community PR from **[@sudoPhoeniX](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-9f32d2b72d51)** was merged into the **Hermes CLI**, with the contributor's approach now the default and the old path moved behind a **--full** flag; the news channel itself logged only routine [automated daily-sync activity](/?date=2026-10-03&category=news#item-2a5ce8ce1c7d) in hermes-agent-community. First-party docs consolidated the week's threads into practical surfaces: running agents on **[Claude Pro/Max](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49790991)** subscription credentials via SDK (extending 1 October's subscription-auth documentation), **[Kanban](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49604068)** multi-agent profile collaboration, **[LanceDB](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49133145)** semantic memory for persistent long-term context, a community **[Grafana](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49318128)** observability stack, and the **[Arduino UNO Q](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49368474)** (4GB RAM, Linux+MCU) as a cheap always-on self-host. On social, **@NousResearch** gave a technical breakdown of **[multi-account](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-efd1eebe7ad7)** Google authentication (per-email token storage), while official replies highlighted agent **[permission control](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-e99c19e5872e)** (the standout reply at 203 likes), [hundreds of selectable models with effort levels](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-5bb9477b2087), and tools exposed via the **[Tool Gateway](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-03971c3e77cb)**. Orchestration momentum held: the **[Codex](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49136162)**↔**Claude Code** skill loop for autonomous issue-to-PR workflows, the **[verso](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49628094)** orchestrator GUI, and **[Almanac](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49511007)** (YC S26) commercializing company-knowledge agents — third parties keep building on Hermes as a platform. Reliability is the sharpest organic thread: a documented [degenerate thinking-loop on Z.ai GLM 5.3 Flash](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49916751) on a headless Debian server, plus community debate over whether a [model router like Bifrost](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49159529) is effectively required for stable operation — caveat: **GLM 5.3 Flash** appears nowhere in the model index (the Z.ai line tops out at **GLM-5.2**), so treat the attribution as unverified — alongside the standing [~23,000 open PRs](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49424643) repo-health caveat, now in its third cycle, and **Teknium** transparently acknowledging [Windows updater slowness](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-946a0d86d668) ([up to 40 minutes for some users](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-92846134c26d)) while framing [recent speedups as only a subset](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-f42a25486ccf) of a larger pending batch. That teaser posture — capped by his cryptic ["What dat means 👀"](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-9e255d992e86) reply (18.7k views, 19 replies) and his usual ["when it's ready"](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-cf834c566206) non-timeline — is fueling genuine anticipation for an upcoming announcement. Community color ran warm: **rlaope** demoed a [Deltarune-themed coding agent on Hermes Desktop](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-f104226b43a6) (helpfully clarifying ["runtime, not fork"](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-6b8093ef1002)), [Hermes was shown running Teknium's personal agent while he was on vacation](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-5e98cda64363), tips covered the [Hermes update terminal command](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-6b20bea16273) and [enabling plugins under the capabilities page](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-85ed75950b2a), and the **[$1 Rebellion Shirt](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-33f8d7228151)** (edition of 2,222) [sold out](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-4db61920a3e8) at 43k views and 535 likes — the cycle's biggest engagement event, with [EU-shipping](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-43c87f3bd202) and [refund](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-adaaffabb767) follow-ups handled by the official account. Governance items below the cut (the [trademark thread](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49357715), the [adversarial-reversal repo](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49231797), the [deleted/blocked-content issue](/?date=2026-10-03&category=research#item-hn-49208206)) were carryovers. Net read: no new model launches, no Reddit threads, and no user-facing news-channel changes this cycle — today's signal is execution and consolidation (rapid RC cadence, a merged community contribution, docs folding the week's patterns into first-party surfaces) ahead of a teased announcement, with reliability — router necessity, updater lag, merge-velocity strain — the metric to watch.

# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-10-03

Executive summary: A release-candidate sprint tops this cycle: Nous Research tagged rc.35 of hermes-agent v0.21.5 on 2026-10-02 roughly 28 minutes after rc.34 — which was immediately superseded, making the real headline the rapid RC cadence ahead of an expected stable v0.21.5 — while the v0.20.0 line (tagged v2026.8.3; announcement title and repo tag still disagree, so verify before pinning) remains the ship of record. The flagship open-source story ran through social rather than the news channel: Teknium confirmed a community PR from @sudoPhoeniX was merged into the Hermes CLI, with the contributor's approach now the default and the old path moved behind a --full flag; the news channel itself logged only routine automated daily-sync activity in hermes-agent-community. First-party docs consolidated the week's threads into practical surfaces: running agents on Claude Pro/Max subscription credentials via SDK (extending 1 October's subscription-auth documentation), Kanban multi-agent profile collaboration, LanceDB semantic memory for persistent long-term context, a community Grafana observability stack, and the Arduino UNO Q (4GB RAM, Linux+MCU) as a cheap always-on self-host. On social, @NousResearch gave a technical breakdown of multi-account Google authentication (per-email token storage), while official replies highlighted agent permission control (the standout reply at 203 likes), hundreds of selectable models with effort levels, and tools exposed via the Tool Gateway. Orchestration momentum held: the Codex↔Claude Code skill loop for autonomous issue-to-PR workflows, the verso orchestrator GUI, and Almanac (YC S26) commercializing company-knowledge agents — third parties keep building on Hermes as a platform. Reliability is the sharpest organic thread: a documented degenerate thinking-loop on Z.ai GLM 5.3 Flash on a headless Debian server, plus community debate over whether a model router like Bifrost is effectively required for stable operation — caveat: GLM 5.3 Flash appears nowhere in the model index (the Z.ai line tops out at GLM-5.2), so treat the attribution as unverified — alongside the standing ~23,000 open PRs repo-health caveat, now in its third cycle, and Teknium transparently acknowledging Windows updater slowness (up to 40 minutes for some users) while framing recent speedups as only a subset of a larger pending batch. That teaser posture — capped by his cryptic "What dat means 👀" reply (18.7k views, 19 replies) and his usual "when it's ready" non-timeline — is fueling genuine anticipation for an upcoming announcement. Community color ran warm: rlaope demoed a Deltarune-themed coding agent on Hermes Desktop (helpfully clarifying "runtime, not fork"), Hermes was shown running Teknium's personal agent while he was on vacation, tips covered the Hermes update terminal command and enabling plugins under the capabilities page, and the $1 Rebellion Shirt (edition of 2,222) sold out at 43k views and 535 likes — the cycle's biggest engagement event, with EU-shipping and refund follow-ups handled by the official account. Governance items below the cut (the trademark thread, the adversarial-reversal repo, the deleted/blocked-content issue) were carryovers. Net read: no new model launches, no Reddit threads, and no user-facing news-channel changes this cycle — today's signal is execution and consolidation (rapid RC cadence, a merged community contribution, docs folding the week's patterns into first-party surfaces) ahead of a teased announcement, with reliability — router necessity, updater lag, merge-velocity strain — the metric to watch.

top_items.title: Belkin killed my smart switch. I got it working again without their app
top_items.content:
I bought a wifi switch from Belkin over 10 years ago, but the app got turned off.

I wanted to use the switch to automate my mosquito repellent. Unfortunately it still had my timer running from Christmas, which meant it turned off too early. It ruined my last night's sleep.

First thing in the morning I opened the app and wanted to change the timer.

The app was offline and I read online that it is discontinued. The switch is basically garbage now.

I was pissed at first, but then I gav

social.category_summary: **Product & Engineering (top of newsletter):** The headline item is **Teknium** [confirming a community PR from **@sudoPhoeniX** was merged into the **Hermes CLI**](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-9f32d2b72d51) — with the contributor's approach now the default and the old behavior moved behind a **--full** flag, a strong open-source-contribution story the community will want flagged. Right behind it, **@NousResearch** gave a [substantive technical breakdown of **multi-account support**](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-efd1eebe7ad7) (one Hermes install authenticating several Google accounts with per-email token storage). Rounding out the capability cluster: official confirmations of [**agent permission control**](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-e99c19e5872e) (the standout reply at 203 likes articulating that Hermes lets you control what your agent accesses and how), [**hundreds of models with selectable effort levels**](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-5bb9477b2087), and [tools already exposed via the **Tool Gateway**](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-03971c3e77cb). **Roadmap & Hype:** **Teknium** [scoped recent improvements as a Windows-only *subset* of a larger batch of changes](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-f42a25486ccf), and his [cryptic 'What dat means 👀' reply](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-9e255d992e86) (18.7k views, 19 replies) is fueling real anticipation for an upcoming Hermes announcement — good 'coming soon' hooks, tempered only by his standard ['when it's ready' non-timeline](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-cf834c566206). **Community Showcases:** **rlaope** [demoed a Deltarune-themed coding agent on **Hermes Desktop**](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-f104226b43a6) (and helpfully [clarified a 'runtime, not fork' distinction](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-6b8093ef1002)), while **Teknium** [playfully confirmed Hermes was running his personal identity/agent while he was on vacation](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-5e98cda64363) — an organic real-world trust signal the community loved. **Tips & Support:** Practical guidance included [running the **Hermes update** terminal command](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-6b20bea16273) and [enabling plugins under the capabilities page](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-85ed75950b2a). **Merch & Brand:** The [**$1 Rebellion Shirt** limited drop (edition of 2222)](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-33f8d7228151) went viral and [sold out](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-4db61920a3e8) — 43k views and 535 likes on the sellout post, the biggest engagement event of the period, with follow-up questions on [EU shipping subsidies](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-43c87f3bd202) and [refunds](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-adaaffabb767) all handled by the official account. **Pain Points:** Honest acknowledgment from **Teknium** that [the updater was significantly slower on Windows](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-946a0d86d668) ([up to 40 minutes for some users](/?date=2026-10-03&category=social#item-92846134c26d)) drew mild grumbling but was met with transparency. **Overall sentiment:** Highly engaged and warm — a community proud of merged contributions, eager for the next drop (both merch and software), playfully bantering with the founders, and forgiving of the updater hiccup given the visible pace of development.
